object_description: transverse, slightly projecting symmetrical wing, flat and expansive between two protected buildings
geometry_property: ground floor as base with set-back classroom floor
folded gable roof with many skylights
design_condition: the new wing lies transversely between the two protected school buildings at a pleasant distance that lets the outdoor spaces flow, clearly subordinating itself to the inventoried buildings

positive: The pleasant distance from the existing buildings allows a flow of the outdoor spaces
Compared to the protected buildings the new wing appears flat and expansive
The volume is clearly and respectfully subordinated to the inventoried buildings
This creates an urbanistically convincing, neighbourhood-friendly ensemble
The new building appears light and transparent
The ground floor becomes the formal base of the elaborately designed classroom floor
The extension almost to the street creates differentiated outdoor spaces
Sports fields lie to the north and a quiet protected play area beside the historic gardens to the west
Parking and delivery are ideally located along the northern boundary
The sunken gymnasium, illuminated on three sides, is extremely atmospheric and works well
It has the required audience area and its cloakrooms can also serve the existing hall
The covered entrance area also serves as an outdoor hall
The classroom floor is reached via a representative, spacious outside staircase
The clear, concentrated form of the learning landscape is convincing
The connected, well-structured corridor zone and surrounding classrooms are alternately lit with skylights
This creates a bright, pleasant studio atmosphere throughout the learning landscape
The gymnasium is supported by a truss on the ceiling allowing a column-free ground floor
The roof construction is proposed in wood, allowing ecological goals to be achieved
In terms of costs the project is within the forecast target costs
The urban design of the flat volume respecting the historical buildings convinced the jury
The high spatial quality of the sports hall and the varied learning landscape particularly distinguish the entry
negative: The concrete frames, suspended classroom floor and folded gable roof cannot establish the formal connection to the historic buildings
The proposed new tree planting on the large break area obscures the protected composition inadmissibly
The covered entrance hall is rather too small for the entire school complex
The functionally desired two-part cluster structure has not been proven on the classroom floor
The project is designed quite spaciously, resulting in about 10 per cent additional area
